newsitem.title: PERU: Japan must authorize any attack on embassy - Perez.
newsitem.headline: Japan must authorize any attack on embassy - Perez.

text.p: Japan must give permission for any eventual Peruvian assault on the embattled embassy residence where Marxist rebels are holding around 340 hostages, former United Nations secretary-general Javier Perez de Cuellar said on Saturday.

"Under international conventions, that building of the embassy is inviolable," Perez de Cuellar told local radio station Radio Programas. "That means the Peruvian government has no possibility whatsoever of entering by military or police means ... without the authorisation of the Japanese government."

Lima has so far rejected all the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement's (MRTA) demands, sparking speculation that an assault on the besieged building might be chosen as the option to end the four-day-old standoff. The government says it hopes for a peaceful solution.

Perez de Cuellar, a Peruvian diplomat who held the U.N.'s top job from 1981-1991, said the international status of the residence and the Japanese nationality of some of the hostages obliged the Lima government to stay in close touch with Tokyo over the crisis.

Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda has been in Peru since Thursday to monitor the situation and liase with the government. Apart from a brief meeting with Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori on arrival, he has spent most of his time with other diplomats or members of the large Japanese community here.
